comment: Disk tree for the DYNAMIC-USERLAND GATE (run.sh dynamic).
Differs from manifest.json in exactly three intentional ways.
1. /sbin/launchd is the static exec-runner work/init_exec, which
execve()s the dylib-linked /bin/echo.  That is the point of the gate:
manifest.json's PID 1 execs nothing, so the standard boot cannot
observe dyld, the libSystem closure or a dylib main().
2. BOTH EFI paths -- System/Library/CoreServices/BOOT.EFI and
EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI -- are the fresh source-built apple-free loader
work/efi/BOOTX64.EFI, not the gitignored assets/ copies, which went
stale and caused the pre-kernel failure in BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.10.
3. /usr/lib/dyld is the freshly source-built MH_DYLINKER at
../../Libraries/dyld/dyld/dyld, not the assets/ copy, which is a
DYLIB (988088 bytes).  The kernel rejects a DYLIB as the dynamic
linker before dyld runs at all, with OS_REASON_EXEC /
EXEC_EXIT_REASON_BAD_MACHO -- see BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.6, where the
throwaway probe that proved this staging path was left in work/ and
never promoted here.  The built image is filetype MH_DYLINKER with
0 LC_LOAD_DYLIB and, as of 2026-10-01, 0 undefined symbols and 0
chained BIND fixups -- the bootstrap-dylinker invariant that a
dylinker is mapped before anything is bound, so it must carry zero
imports.  See BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.7.
Any other divergence between the two trees is a bug in this file, not
a feature.
The 'init_exec' marker makes mkimage.py select work/init_exec.
PROVENANCE SWEEP (PROVENANCE-PLAN P0 change 2, 2026-10-02).
Three entries were removed or repointed, and two more were dropped
because the repo-built closure cannot satisfy them.  The "glob" over
assets/usr/lib/system/ is GONE: it staged all 46 files in that
directory, 31 of which were extracted from the host Mac's dyld shared
cache and 28 of which failed dyld2's LINKEDIT validation
(exports_trie=(0,0) against a nonzero __LINKEDIT.fileoff), so the
image this manifest described could not have loaded.  The 27 members
of the repo-built closure are now named one by one, and
usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib -- itself host-extracted -- is now the repo
build product that roots them.  See manifest_cpmv.json for the same
closure: 46 explicit entries, 0 absolute paths, and as of 2026-10-02
0 entries that leave the repository either.  libunwind.dylib and
libcompiler_rt.dylib are both repo-built by Libraries/Libsystem/Makefile
(the libunwind.dylib and libcompiler_rt.dylib targets), which link into
${.CURDIR} and install to the SDK.  libcompiler_rt.dylib previously had
no producer at all; see the target for how its 529-name export surface is
derived from the vendored compiler-rt sources.
usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib  repointed from the host-extracted asset to
../../Libraries/Libsystem/libSystem.B.dylib.
bin/ls   "asset": LC_LOAD_DYLIB names /usr/lib/libutil.dylib, which
the repo closure does not build -- an unstaged dependency, so
dyld would have stopped there.
bin/cat  "asset": needs _malloc_type_malloc, which the repo-built
libsystem_malloc does not export -- an unresolved non-weak
undefined symbol, so dyld would have failed at bind time.  It
was the last thing between this manifest and a clean closure;
closure_check named it.
usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib  "asset": libobjc is reached ONLY by
LC_LOAD_UPWARD_DYLIB from libdispatch/libxpc/libsystem_trace,
which name it by install name, and those records say
/usr/lib/system/libobjc.dylib -- no LC_LOAD_UPWARD_DYLIB can
resolve to this path.  It is staged inside the closure above.
P1 SWEEP (2026-10-02).  The host binaries this manifest used to stage
out of assets/ are gone from the tree, not merely un-staged.  See
tools/bootlab/assets-quarantine/QUARANTINE_INVENTORY.txt.  Two entries
were repointed and one added:
bin/echo   was assets/bin/echo, an APPLE PRODUCT BINARY copied off
this host's disk.  It is now work/echo_dyn, built from
BSD/bin/echo/echo.c.  Its LC_UUID was never in the host dyld
cache, so provenance_scan.py could not flag it -- it was host
disk product, not a cache extract, and the cache-UUID test is
blind to that case by construction.
bin/sh     was assets/bin/sh, a 4,280-byte freestanding static image
that cannot reach dyld at all.  It is now work/sh_dyn.
usr/lib/libedit.dylib  ADDED, because work/sh_dyn LC_LOAD_DYLIBs it.
This manifest therefore NOW depends on work/ products after all.  The
earlier decision not to -- recorded above -- was made when assets/bin/echo
and assets/bin/sh were the only options and the alternative was an
unstaged dependency.  run_dynamic_gate.sh builds them with
build_dynutils.sh before it builds the image, so the dependency is
satisfied by a producer rather than by an Apple binary.
The image is checked before it is built: closure_gate.py runs
closure_check.py over this exact manifest and refuses to continue on a
nonzero verdict (PROVENANCE-PLAN P2).

files.comment: the loader built from tools/efiloader/ by build_applefree.sh, NOT the gitignored assets/boot.efi, which went stale and produced the pre-kernel failure in BOOT-PLAN sec. 15.10
same build as the CoreServices copy; the old 'asset': 'BOOTX64.EFI' was not our loader at all (SizeOfImage 0x17e2c0, no RL: strings)
static exec-runner; execve()s the dynamic /bin/echo

P1 (2026-10-02): was "asset": "bin/sh".  The assets copy is a 4,280-byte FREESTANDING LC_UNIXTHREAD image with no LC_LOAD_DYLIB at all -- ours, and therefore not quarantined, but it is also not what this gate is for: it cannot exercise dyld, because it never reaches it.  work/sh_dyn is the repo-built dynamic shell (BSD/bin/sh against ../../Libraries/Libsystem/libSystem.B.dylib and ../../BSD/lib/libedit/libedit.dylib), so the fallback init path exercises the same closure the gate is judging.

P1 (2026-10-02): was "asset": "bin/echo", an APPLE PRODUCT BINARY lifted byte-for-byte off this host (universal x86_64+arm64e, LC_CODE_SIGNATURE, LC_LOAD_DYLIB /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib current version 1356.0.0).  Its LC_UUID is not in the host dyld cache, which is exactly why closure_check.py's provenance scan could never have caught it -- it was host DISK product, not a cache extract.  It is now quarantined in tools/bootlab/assets-quarantine/ (see QUARANTINE_INVENTORY.txt sec. 3).  work/echo_dyn is the repo-built dynamic echo (BSD/bin/echo/echo.c against ../../Libraries/Libsystem/libSystem.B.dylib) and is still the subject of this gate: init_exec execve()s /bin/echo, and it LC_LOAD_DYLIBs /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib, so the closure is exercised.
P1 (2026-10-02): added because work/sh_dyn LC_LOAD_DYLIBs it.  Without this entry the closure would have an unstaged dependency and closure_gate.py would refuse.
